extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying for the MRC Senior Non-Clinical Fellowship (applicants and host research offices)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and assessment criteria for preparing and submitting an application to the MRC Senior Non‑Clinical Fellowship (UKRI Funding Service). Covers eligibility, application structure, section-specific assessment expectations, resource justification, partner and host statements, and assessment process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: basic applicant requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: You must have a PhD or equivalent; have experience leading research funded by a major funder; be managing your own independent research group; have the support of an eligible research organisation. There are no eligibility rules based on age or years of postdoctoral experience. International applicants are welcome provided the fellowship is hosted by an eligible UK-based research organisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you're unsure about eligibility, contact fellows@mrc.ukri.org. Note disqualification if you have applied for this MRC fellowship within the last year, have applied twice before, have an application to another UKRI fellowship currently being assessed, or previously held a comparable senior fellowship. You cannot hold a salaried position and a fellowship at the same time (must give up permanent position or change to proleptic appointment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of acceptable research
rubrics_metrics.description: Research may focus on any area of the MRC remit to improve human health, from basic mechanistic studies to translational and developmental clinical research, including interdisciplinary and global health approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Science areas listed include infections and immunity, molecular and cellular medicine, population and systems medicine, neurosciences and mental health, translation, global health, methodology and public health. Requests to fund new longitudinal population studies may be considered but require prior LPS‑SAP approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship purpose and aims
rubrics_metrics.description: The fellowship should support internationally competitive independent researchers to lead an ambitious research programme, pursue research training to develop their career, and make the transition to research leader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must explain why a fellowship is the best support for their long-term career goals, show ambitious and credible ideas for career step-change, and describe experience of managing an independent research group including influencing and supporting others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You must identify at least one sponsor who is a senior member of the department hosting the fellowship, acts as a supporter (not supervisor), has expertise in the research area and acts as guarantor for the quality of the proposed work, and the suitability of you as a fellowship candidate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional sponsors can be named if necessary; sponsor costs may only be requested in exceptional circumstances (should not exceed 5% of their time or 5% FTE across sponsors) and must be entered as directly allocated staff cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding available and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no limit on the amount of funding you can apply for. MRC will fund 80% of the full economic cost (FEC) and will cover 50% of the cost of your salary for up to five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We expect fellows to take advantage of full five years where appropriate. Sponsor costs only in exceptional circumstances. Requests for support beyond PDRA and technical posts only in exceptional circumstances and must be discussed with the office in advance. Up to 12 months can be spent at a second organisation (UK, overseas, or industry); longer overseas periods should be discussed with programme manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs we will not fund
rubrics_metrics.description: MRC will not fund costs for PhD studentships, publication costs, funding to use as a 'bridge' between grants, or costs for mentors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the full list in the 'What we will not fund' section before requesting these items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team project partners: inclusion and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: You may include project partners who support the fellowship through cash or in‑kind contributions (staff time, access to equipment, data, sites, recruitment, samples). Project partners must provide a statement of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A core team member (including other departments within same organisation) cannot be a project partner. Project partners that are industry must provide additional information under the Industry Collaboration Framework (ICF). For audit purposes formal collaboration agreements will be required if an award is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project partner letters of support: format and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Project partner letters/emails of support must be uploaded as a single PDF containing each partner's letter/email; each must be no more than two A4 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should confirm commitment, explain value/relevance/benefits, describe additional value they bring, include organisation and contact info (matching the entry in the Funding Service). Not required to be on headed paper or have handwritten signatures; electronic signatures acceptable. Consolidate multiple partners into one PDF not exceeding 8MB. File name must use Funding Service number + 'Project partner'. Do not include letters from core team members; including unrequested information may cause rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core team roles and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: List key members and assign roles from provided list (specialist, professional enabling staff, research and innovation associate, technician, fellow). Only one individual may be listed as fellow; you must list at least one sponsor and assign them as professional enabling staff. Mentors should not be listed in the core team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you include more than one fellow your application will fail the checks. Ensure research office and host organisation are aware of the application and that the lead research organisation will submit the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Summary: public plain-English requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a plain-English summary (550 words) suitable to identify experts to assess the application; summaries may be made publicly available so must not include confidential or sensitive information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly describe context, the challenge addressed, aims and objectives, potential applications and benefits. Make it suitable for a range of readers including policymakers, public, and research community.

rubrics_metrics.name: References guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications should be self-contained; references should be included in the appropriate question section and be easily identifiable (e.g., (Smith, Research Paper, 2019)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use persistent identifiers (DOIs) where possible. Assessors are not required to access links; do not include links to web resources to extend your application. Use discretion and prioritise most pertinent references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image usage and file format rules
rubrics_metrics.description: You may demonstrate elements of some responses in visual form if relevant, but images must be used sparingly and only to convey important information that cannot easily be put into words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert each new image on its own line, provide a descriptive legend immediately underneath (legend counts towards word limit). File types allowed: JPEG, JPG, JPE, JFI, JIF, JFIF, PNG, GIF, BMP, WEBP. Files must be smaller than 5MB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vision section assessment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Vision (550 words): explain what you are hoping to achieve with the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors look for whether the proposed work is of excellent quality and importance within or beyond the field; potential to advance understanding or generate new knowledge; timeliness given trends/context; impact on research, society, economy or environment. Also identify beneficiaries, improvements in human/population health, and outline engagement, communication and dissemination plans. Visuals and references may be included in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach section assessment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach (6,050 words): explain how you will deliver the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors look for effective and appropriate design to achieve objectives; feasibility with risks identified and mitigations; clearly written transparent methodology; summary of previous work and how proposed work builds on it; maximising translation into outcomes/impacts. Additionally, demonstrate access to services/facilities/equipment; provide detailed project plan with milestones/timelines (chart or diagram); explain collaborations and work at second host (if applicable); include diversity and inclusion approaches for study populations; justify use/non-use of both sexes in animal research. You are encouraged to include a 500-word 'Reproducibility and statistical design' addition covering statistical analyses, sample/effect sizes, models, and methods; seek professional statistical advice. If animal sample size/statistics are in Approach, do not duplicate in the 'Research involving animals' section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility and statistical design guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 500 words labelled 'Reproducibility and statistical design' to provide information on reliability and robustness, such as statistical analyses, experimental design and sample sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only use this space for reproducibility/statistical design; if not applicable do not use it to expand other areas. Seek professional statistical advice. Include experimental approach to objectives, sample/effect sizes, planned statistical analyses, chosen models (animal model, cell line) and other relevant details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development section assessment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Career development (1,000 words): explain why this fellowship is the right way to develop your career and how you will use it to benefit others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors expect identification of career development goals appropriate to the fellowship; how the fellowship provides a feasible appropriate trajectory; how you will instigate positive change in wider research/innovation community (EDI, advocacy, peer review, policy influence, public engagement). Also describe how you will ensure development opportunities for those you manage (links to Concordat and Technician Commitment provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant capability to deliver (R4RI format) criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant capability (1,650 words; 1,150 words R4RI modules plus optional 500-word additions): explain why you are the right person to deliver the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors look for evidence of relevant experience appropriate to career stage; the right balance of skills and aptitude; contributions to developing a positive research environment and wider community; teamworking/leadership skills. Use Résumé for Research and Innovation (R4RI) format with module headings: contributions to generation of new ideas/tools/methodologies/knowledge; development of others and effective working relationships; contributions to the wider research & innovation community; contributions to broader research/innovation users and societal benefit. Optional 500-word 'Additions' may explain contextual factors (e.g., career breaks) but should not repeat skills/outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host organisation support statement criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Host organisation support (1,000 words): head of department must provide a supporting statement written by them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement must include name/title of head of department, evidence of how host will support you (career development, vision/approach), how research environment contributes to success, how time commitment to fellowship will be protected, development/training opportunities forming a cohesive package, financial/practical support (services, facilities, infrastructure, equipment), evidence of your suitability for MRC fellowship, and details of fellowship work at another host (if applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Second host organisation support statement criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Second host organisation support (1,000 words): where fellowship includes a second host (another research organisation or industry), the appropriate head-equivalent must provide a supporting statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement should mirror host support content: name/title, evidence of support for career development and vision, contribution of research environment, protection of time commitment, training opportunities, financial/practical support. If not applicable mark N/A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous head of department support statement
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, provide a support statement (1,000 words) from your previous head of department assessing your suitability for an MRC fellowship when you have recently moved department or will undertake the fellowship elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not applicable indicate N/A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor statements: required content and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors (up to 3,000 words total; individual sponsor statements up to 1,000 words) must provide statements supporting the applicant and detailing their relationship and endorsement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each sponsor entry should include sponsor name and current position, how they know you and for how long, views on your research ability and suitability for the fellowship, measures of research activity where you will be based (e.g., number of academic staff), and the suitability and quality of support/training you will receive and how your research fits the research environment. Sponsor is not expected to act as supervisor but as guarantor for quality of research and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentoring arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentors (500 words): explain proposed mentoring arrangements. If a mentor is identified they should be named and provide a statement of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how mentorship will operate during the fellowship and how it will support career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project partners: details to include
rubrics_metrics.description: For each project partner include organisation name, contact name and email, type of contribution (direct or indirect) and its monetary value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project partners should not be core team members. Project partners are not usually expected to receive funds, but minor costs (e.g., travel/subsistence) may be claimed and justified in the resources section. For partners responsible for recruitment or human tissue supply, letters must confirm suitability and quantity appropriate but not excessive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry Collaboration Framework (ICF) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If your application includes industry project partners you must complete the ICF section (1,500 words) and follow the ICF decision tree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors expect description of the nature, goals and conditions of the collaboration, any restrictions/rights to results, classification as basic or applied research, whether contribution is fully flexible or gated, background IP each partner brings and terms of access, expected foreground IP and management (ownership, use rights, academic partner commercialisation rights). Include ICF documentation, collaboration agreements and consider subsidy control. Repeat ICF responses for each ICF project partner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research involving human participants
rubrics_metrics.description: If the project involves human subjects or personal information (700 words), provide name of required approving body and whether approval is in place; justify number and diversity of participants and any procedures; provide details of any areas of substantial or moderate severity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not applicable indicate N/A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research involving human tissues or biological samples
rubrics_metrics.description: If research involves human tissues/biological samples (700 words), provide name of required approving body and whether approval is in place; justify nature and quantity of material and its source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not applicable indicate N/A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research involving animals: overview and data duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: If your project involves animals, provide rationale for use, choice of species, welfare considerations, procedure severity and any sample size/statistical analyses information (use Approach section for sample size/statistics to avoid duplication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If animal sample sizes/statistical analyses are presented in Approach, do not duplicate them in the 'Research involving the use of animals' section. Follow MRC guidance for animal research and justify use of sexes in animal/tissue studies or provide justification for not using both sexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources and cost justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources and cost justification (1,000 words): justify the application's more costly resources and confirm they are comprehensive, appropriate and justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on project staff, significant travel for fieldwork/collaboration, equipment >£10,000, consumables beyond typical requirements, facilities/infrastructure costs, training, items costed as 'Exceptions', support for second organisation, public and patient involvement and engagement, data preservation/sharing, NHS research costs, animal costs, and sponsor support (<=5% time). Assessors are not looking for a line-by-line budget but that resources represent optimal use to achieve outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical research using NHS resources and SoECAT requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For clinical research involving the NHS or Health and Social Care duty of care (250 words), you must complete a SoECAT to be eligible for the NIHR RDN portfolio and to allow attribution of excess treatment costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: contact an AcoRD specialist early; complete online SoECAT; request authorisation; extract 'study information' and 'summary' from the funder export, combine into single PDF and upload; ensure AcoRD specialist's name and date are included. Applications requiring SoECAT but not attaching authorised export may be rejected. Contact fellows@mrc.ukri.org for UKRI aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related applications and resubmission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Related applications (500 words): disclose if application is related to another application to MRC or other funder; you are allowed to apply to other funders concurrently but must declare related submissions. If resubmitting include previous MRC reference number and explain differences and how feedback was addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may only apply twice for any MRC fellowship regardless of changes to the application; changing organisation or project does not reset the count.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment process and stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are assessed by independent peer review, shortlisting by an expert panel using comments/scores, and shortlisted applicants are invited to interview. Interview panel makes funding recommendation; MRC makes final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants cannot nominate reviewers on the new Funding Service. If shortlisted you will be sent reviews and can respond during interview; if not shortlisted you will receive review comments as feedback but cannot respond. Interviews for non-clinical training and career development panel usually last 30 minutes; MRC contributes to travel subsistence and reasonable family care costs. Aim to complete assessment within six months; shortlisting decisions and interview dates are provided on timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment areas and explicit review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment areas used by reviewers: vision for the fellowship; approach to the fellowship (including data management); career development; applicant capability to deliver (skills and experience expected at this career stage); support for the applicant; ethical and responsible research & innovation considerations; and resources requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will take into account career breaks, flexible working and changes in discipline when assessing career development and capability. Senior non-clinical fellowship applicants are considered in open competition with career development award (CDA) applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission and institutional responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are made via the UKRI Funding Service: the fellow is responsible for completing the application but the lead research organisation must submit it. Research offices must check and submit the completed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the lead organisation is NHS check it is available in the Funding Service early; allow at least 10 working days for adding an organisation. Create an organisation Administration Account to manage acceptance and grant management. Save answers in text boxes or work offline and paste in. Allow time to check application in 'read-only' view before sending to research office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting, upload and file-size restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Files and images included in the Funding Service have file type and size limits: images <=5MB and specific image formats; project partner PDF <=8MB; project partner letters max two A4 pages each; legends and supporting text count towards word limits where specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert images on separate lines with legends immediately beneath. Follow Funding Service upload instructions and naming conventions (e.g., Funding Service number + 'Project partner'). Including unrequested information may lead to application rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of assessment and research integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: MRC/UKRI support the San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA) and UKRI principles of assessment and decision making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors will be guided by these principles and by guidance on considering career breaks and flexible working to ensure fair assessment. UKRI reserves the right to modify assessment processes as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback and timing of decision communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants will be informed of decisions within specified timescales: aim to communicate decisions within 10 days of the shortlisting panel meeting; feedback procedures differ by stage (reviews provided if not shortlisted or after interview).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not shortlisted you receive review comments (no response). If interviewed you will receive reviews and panel reasons; MRC aims to complete assessment within six months of application receipt. Specific timeline dates are published on the opportunity page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitive/confidential information handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicants or core team members need to convey confidential information (e.g., unavailable dates, declarations of interest, eligibility nuances) they should email fellows@mrc.ukri.org with subject line indicating sensitive information and Funding Service application number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical examples include parental leave dates, declaration of interest, additional eligibility context, conflicts of interest for reviewer/panel selection, invited resubmission. See UKRI privacy notice for how personal data are handled. Joint funder applications will require sharing application and personal information with co‑funders for assessment.
